posts.title: 跟著水圳去「夜巡」！2026東興圳光藝節12/5–12/27竹北登場：每晚17:30點燈、免費入場，四週主題市集從人氣小吃吃到聖誕手作
posts.body:
冬天的夜晚有點冷，但新竹竹北有一條被燈光點亮的水圳，很適合穿暖暖慢慢散步。活動時間和逛法整理給你：
在竹北的高樓和新社區之間，有一條安靜流過的水圳：東興圳。很多人每天沿著它散步、遛狗、騎腳踏車，卻不一定知道，它曾經是灌溉六家地區農田的重要大圳。

今年冬天，這條水圳要在夜裡發光了。「2026 東興圳光藝節」將於 12 月 5 日到 12 月 27 日在東興圳公園登場，每天 17:30–21:30 點燈，免費入場。

【「夜巡・探水光」：一個關於水圳的溫柔故事】

根據官方網站的策展理念，本屆主題是「夜巡・探水光（Tam Shui Gong）」，策展人為江政樺。在水圳還用來灌溉的年代，農人會在夜裡巡圳、巡田水，維護灌溉秩序，也防範竊盜與動物侵擾。水圳的夜晚，其實是萬物活絡的時刻。

「探水光」來自客語羅馬拼音：Tam 是「探」，有查訪、走近理解的意思；Shui 是水，也是田水；Gong 既是「光」，也是「講」。過去的光照亮夜巡的路，今天的光則用來講述故事。官方邀請大家依照自己的步伐行走、停留、觀看，重新認識這條陪伴城市生活的水圳。

【四週主題市集，每個週末都不一樣】

官方公告的市集安排如下：

・第一週 12/5（六）–12/6（日）：「流光序曲 × 光聚派對」，以開幕慶典為主軸，集合人氣餐車與創意小吃（12/5 14:00–21:00、12/6 14:00–20:00）。
・第二週 12/12（六）–12/13（日）：與「友の市」合作的風格生活市集，有插畫、手作工藝、質感選物與特色餐飲（14:00–20:00）。
・第三週 12/18（五）–12/20（日）：「風味食集」，美食當主角（12/18 16:00–20:00，12/19–20 14:00–20:00）。
・第四週 12/25（五）–12/27（日）：「好好手感聖誕市集」，集合原創手作與設計品牌，為光藝節畫下溫暖句點（12/25–26 15:00–20:00，12/27 13:00–18:00）。

官方也提醒，實際出攤攤位以活動當日現場為準。開幕點燈訂於 12 月 5 日晚間，演出細節請追蹤新竹縣政府文化局官方粉專。

【交通怎麼去？】

・地點：東興圳公園（新竹縣竹北市文興路），官方特別提醒「非文興路二段」。
・公車：可搭新竹縣市區公車快捷 9 號至「縣立總圖書館」站；或搭公路客運 5615 至「縣體育場」，再步行或騎 YouBike 約 650 公尺；新竹市 182 路至「文興嘉興路口」，步行約 600 公尺。
・高鐵：官方建議可由高鐵新竹站轉乘快捷公車至文興路口。
・開車：周邊有「停18」（莊敬南路與成功十一街）與體育場停車場，假日人多，建議多利用大眾運輸。

【給第一次去的人：怎麼逛最舒服？】

東興圳公園是沿著水圳延伸的帶狀公園，建議不要急著一次走完，可以把它當作一段「散步路線」：先在入口附近吃點市集小吃暖暖身，再順著水流慢慢往前走，每遇到一件光藝作品就停下來看一看、拍幾張照，累了就找張椅子坐著聽水聲。帶小朋友的家庭，可以玩「找光」小遊戲，看誰先發現下一件作品；喜歡拍照的人，則可以試著把水面倒影一起拍進畫面裡。

【夜巡小提醒】

・請勿觸摸、攀爬光藝作品，也不要使用強力手電筒或雷射光，以免干擾作品。
・水岸夜晚風大，記得帶外套、圍巾；帶小朋友的話，留意水邊安全。
・垃圾請帶走或投入指定回收點，讓水圳保持乾淨。

【Cute News 想說】

一條水圳，從灌溉稻田到陪伴城市散步，默默流過了好幾代人的生活。今年 12 月，不妨在下班後或週末傍晚，像從前的農人一樣，沿著水流慢慢走一段「夜巡」路線：看看光、吃點小吃、聽聽水聲，你會發現，竹北的冬夜原來這麼溫柔。

Q：2026 東興圳光藝節什麼時候？要門票嗎？
A：2026 年 12 月 5 日至 12 月 27 日，每日 17:30–21:30 點燈，地點在新竹縣竹北市東興圳公園（文興路），免費入場。

Q：東興圳光藝節有市集嗎？
A：有，共四週主題市集：12/5–6 開幕美食派對、12/12–13 風格生活市集、12/18–20 風味食集、12/25–27 好好手感聖誕市集，攤位以現場為準。

Q：怎麼搭大眾運輸到東興圳公園？
A：可搭新竹縣快捷 9 號到「縣立總圖書館」站，或搭 5615 至「縣體育場」再步行約 650 公尺，也可由高鐵新竹站轉乘快捷公車前往。

posts.body:
最近看到很多人在問：「烏龍茶酒桶威士忌」到底是在威士忌裡面加茶嗎？還是桶子本身有茶味？剛好龐尼維爾官網對這支酒的做法寫得蠻清楚，這篇就用比較口語的方式整理一下，順便聊聊喝法。內容都是照官網說明，不是我自己的心得，有錯再請大家指正。

【先講結論：不是在威士忌裡泡茶葉】

這款酒的重點在「桶子」。官網的說明是：先用台灣的優質烏龍茶，做成一款烏龍茶酒（茶的 liqueur），把這款茶酒放進精選的橡木桶裡熟成。等到桶子吸收了茶酒的味道之後，把已經熟成的單一麥芽威士忌換進這些桶子裡做第二段熟成，也就是「過桶」（finish）。

所以整個流程可以拆成兩步：

1. 茶酒入桶：烏龍茶酒在橡木桶裡熟成，官網說這個過程會讓桶子帶上單寧、蜂蜜般的甜味，還有淡淡的煙燻感。
2. 威士忌過桶：熟成好的單一麥芽威士忌再進到這些「吸飽茶酒」的桶子，慢慢吸收茶的細緻風味。

官網也提到，這個做法是參考傳統雪莉桶的概念：用別種酒先潤桶，再讓威士忌過桶，讓風味多一層。

【官方描述的風味】

官網的品飲描述大概是這樣：

・外觀：金琥珀色。
・香氣：熟果、太妃糖、烘烤堅果、淡淡橡木，混著花香茶香，還有一點烘烤茶葉的氣味。
・口感：質地滑順，有麥芽的甜，也有烏龍茶的花香與木質感，帶一點點煙燻。
・尾韻：茶味的餘韻，加上橡木帶來的溫暖感。

標示的關鍵字是「熟果、太妃糖、烘烤堅果、橡木與花香」，以及「橡木、麥芽與茶」。看起來走的是「麥芽甜感為底，茶香當配角」的路線，而不是整杯都是茶味。

【兩個版本有什麼不同】

官網目前有兩個烏龍茶酒桶版本：

・｜烏龍茶酒桶 40%｜烏龍茶酒桶 原桶強度
・容量｜700 ml｜670 ml
・酒精濃度｜40%｜52.3%
・基酒｜單一麥芽｜單一麥芽
・桶型｜烏龍茶酒桶過桶｜烏龍茶酒桶過桶

[圖片 2]

兩款的描述同樣是「熟果、太妃糖、烘烤堅果、橡木與花香」，差別主要在濃度：原桶強度沒有加水稀釋，酒精感和風味濃度自然比較高。如果是第一次接觸，通常比較建議先從 40% 的開始；已經習慣烈一點的酒，再去比較原桶強度版。

【想試試看，可以怎麼喝】

下面是比較通用的喝法建議，不是官方指定：

・純飲或加一小塊冰：先聞聞看有沒有官網說的花香與烘烤茶葉味，再喝喝看麥芽甜感和茶香怎麼搭。
・原桶強度版加幾滴水：加一點點水常常能讓香氣更容易打開，可以一滴一滴慢慢加，找到自己舒服的比例。
・搭點心：既然是帶茶香和堅果感的酒，搭堅果、不太甜的點心，或烘焙過的茶點，風味方向比較接近，不容易互相蓋過去。

【跟其他茶酒桶系列的關係】

龐尼維爾的「酒桶系列」不只烏龍茶。官網的酒款列表裡還有茉莉綠茶、草莓、桑葚、青梅、玫瑰、荔枝、蜂蜜、金棗、檸檬、橘子、黑后與金香葡萄等酒桶系列，概念都是先用台灣的水果、茶或花入酒，再用那個桶子給威士忌過桶。有興趣的人可以把不同酒桶的描述放在一起看，會比較容易理解「同一款基酒，換一種桶會差在哪裡」。

【順手補充：這家酒廠的基本資料】

・酒廠位在桃園龜山的「兔子坑」，2004 年 7 月 15 日取得製酒執照，算是台灣第一代民營酒廠（2002–2004 年核照）。
・官網公布的蒸餾設備：壺式蒸餾器 6 座（3,000／2,000／2,000／1,000／1,000／200L），加上 2 座柱式蒸餾塔（7 公尺 20 層泡罩、9 公尺 32 層泡罩）。
・官方寫的蒸餾產能是一年 100 萬瓶。
・實體門市在台北大安區永康街 13 巷 1 號，想實際看酒款可以先查官網的營業資訊。

【小結】

烏龍茶酒桶威士忌的特色，是「用茶酒潤過的桶子」來做第二段熟成，而不是直接加茶。如果你本來就喜歡有點花香、堅果和太妃糖氣息的威士忌，這類酒款滿值得拿來比較看看。大家如果有喝過其他家的茶桶或類似做法的酒，也歡迎留言分享，這邊就當作交流。

（以上品飲描述皆為酒廠官網的官方說明，並非獨立評論。）

posts.title: Pot still vs column still, and what a 7 m / 20-plate and a 9 m / 32-plate column are for: using one Taiwanese distillery's published specs
posts.body:
I saw a few threads recently asking why distilleries list things like "7 metres, 20 plates" on their spec sheets, and what that actually tells you about the spirit. Most distilleries don't publish much, so I used one that does — Bunnyville Distillery in Taoyuan, Taiwan — as a worked example. Everything about the distillery below comes from its own website; the general distilling explanation is the standard textbook version, and I'll mark where the two meet.

## Pot stills vs column stills in one paragraph

A **pot still** is a batch machine: you fill it, heat it, run it, and empty it. Because it makes a relatively low-strength separation in each run, it keeps a lot of the character of what went in, which is why pot stills are the classic tool for malt whisky. A **column still** (also called a continuous or Coffey still) is a tall column with plates stacked inside. Vapour rises and condenses on the plates again and again, so every plate acts like a small extra distillation. The more plates (and the taller the column), the more separation you get and the lighter and cleaner the spirit tends to be.

## What Bunnyville publishes

Per the distillery's "Our Distillery" page, the distillation equipment is:

- **Pot stills: 6** — 3,000 L, 2,000 L, 2,000 L, 1,000 L, 1,000 L and 200 L.
- **Column stills: 2** — one 7 m tall with 20 bubble-cap plates, and one 9 m tall with 32 bubble-cap plates.

The distillery is in the "Rabbit Hole" (兔子坑) area of Guishan, Taoyuan, and was licensed on July 15, 2004, making it one of Taiwan's first-generation private distilleries (licensed 2002–2004). It states a distilling capacity of one million bottles per year.

## 7 m / 20 plates vs 9 m / 32 plates

Here is the part that is explained on the distillery's site: a column with more plates gives higher separation and a cleaner spirit, while the 20-plate column preserves more of the aroma of the raw material. That lines up with the general principle above. So, as a rule of thumb:

| | 7 m, 20 plates | 9 m, 32 plates |
|---|---|---|
| Separation | Lower | Higher |
| Spirit character | Keeps more raw-material aroma | Cleaner |
| Use it when you want... | Flavour to carry through | A lighter, neutral base |

I want to be careful here: the site does not say which column feeds which product, so I'm not going to claim that a given bottle came from a given column. The table is the general trade-off, and the distillery's own sentence about plates is the only specific claim.

## Why a distillery would want both

Having two columns of different height gives you a choice of how far to push a spirit. A short column with fewer plates is closer to a "flavourful" spirit, and a tall column with many plates is closer to neutral. Add six pot stills ranging from 200 L up to 3,000 L, and you can see why a distillery would run several styles at once. The big pots are suited to larger batches, and a 200 L pot is the kind of size you would use for small trial runs. That last part is my inference from the sizes, not something the distillery states.

## Where this shows up in the bottles

The distillery's product pages mention a few things that connect to this:

- **No.17 single grain whisky** is made from wheat, aged in charred virgin American white oak, and described by the distillery as smooth and accessible, with floral and honey aroma and apple, lemon and hazelnut on the palate. Single grain whisky is commonly made with column distillation, but the page doesn't specify the still, so treat that connection as general background.
- **The single malts**, such as No.19, and the tea- and fruit-barrel finishes (for example the oolong tea barrel finish) are described as single malts finished in casks previously seasoned with a tea or fruit liqueur.

[Image 2]

## How to read a distillery spec sheet

If you want to compare distilleries, here are some practical questions to ask whenever a spec sheet lists stills:

1. **Pot or column?** Pot suggests more character per run; column suggests a lighter spirit.
2. **How many plates?** More plates generally means cleaner spirit.
3. **What sizes?** Larger stills mean larger batches; very small stills tend to be for experiments or small releases.
4. **Is capacity stated as bottles, litres or number of stills?** These aren't directly comparable, so be careful with any ranking that mixes them.

If you have a spec sheet from another distillery, I'd be curious how its still lineup compares. And if anyone with distilling experience wants to correct my plain-language summary above, please do.

*Facts about the distillery are from Bunnyville's own website; the general distilling explanation is standard background, not claims specific to the distillery.*

posts.title: 秋冬的飲料杯都變紫色了！紫玉甘薯、厚蜜地瓜咖啡接力登場：從手搖飲到拉麵，台灣人把「地瓜」喝成冬天最可愛的甜點
posts.body:
想像一下，在雲霧繚繞的高山上，抬頭就能看到發光的耶誕樹。今年的梨山燈光節，把這個畫面搬到海拔將近兩千公尺的山城，以下是時間、交通和保暖的重點整理。
如果你最近走進手搖飲店或咖啡店，大概會發現菜單上多了好多「紫色」和「地瓜色」。天氣一轉涼，台灣人對地瓜的愛就藏不住了：從路邊的烤地瓜，到杯子裡綿綿的薯泥，冬天的甜味好像都從土裡長出來。

【手搖飲變紫色：台農 73 號「紫玉甘薯」登場】

根據《食尚玩家》報導，手搖品牌「特好喝」11 月 19 日起推出 7 款「紫玉系列」新品，選用台灣在地的台農 73 號紫玉甘薯，把綿密的薯泥和紫玉奶蓋，搭配茉莉綠茶、蕎麥、抹茶和鮮奶。

其中「紫玉三茉」帶著茉莉花香，中杯 80 元、大杯 90 元；「紫玉抹茶」則用抹茶的微苦平衡地瓜甜味，中杯 70 元起；另外還有偏濃郁的「輕潤奶」系列、覆上奶蓋的「紫玉抹茶沙沙」，以及冷熱都可以的「紫玉鮮奶」。層層堆疊的紫色，看起來就像一杯可以喝的蒙布朗。

【脆上討論度高的「厚蜜地瓜」咖啡】

另一邊，CAMA CAFE 的「厚蜜地瓜」系列，則是在 Threads 上引起不少討論。把烤地瓜的香甜融進咖啡裡，有人覺得是冬天限定的驚喜，也有人好奇「地瓜加美式到底是什麼味道」。品牌共推出 3 款地瓜系列飲品，報導指出預計販售到年底，11 月底前也有任選兩杯 88 折的優惠。

【連拉麵都「芋」起來】

根莖類的甜味不只出現在飲料杯裡。上報報導，拉麵品牌麵屋武藏推出冬季限定企劃，光復店的「紫芋鴨白湯拉麵」把芋泥和酥炸芋絲放進湯裡，還貼心提供「去芋頭」選項；信義店則有加入地瓜奶油的「金薯奶油煮干濃湯拉麵」。地瓜和芋頭在冬天的人氣，真的很難擋。

如果想嚐鮮，建議先從中杯、少糖開始，因為薯泥本身就帶有自然甜味；喜歡清爽口感的人可以選茶底，偏愛濃郁的人則可以選鮮奶系列。熱門新品在下午時段比較容易排隊，提早點單或用 App 預訂會更從容。

【為什麼台灣人冬天特別愛地瓜？】

地瓜是台灣人很有感情的食物。早年它是填飽肚子的主食，現在則是健康又療癒的點心。秋冬氣溫下降，地瓜經過烤、蒸之後，香氣和甜味會更明顯，捧在手上熱熱的，就像握住一個小暖爐。紫色地瓜的顏色又特別夢幻，拍照也很可愛，難怪成了今年秋冬的話題食材。

【在家也能做：簡單版地瓜牛奶】

・蒸地瓜：把紫地瓜或黃地瓜洗淨去皮切塊，用電鍋蒸到筷子可以輕鬆穿過。
・壓成泥：趁熱用湯匙壓碎，喜歡甜一點可以加少許黑糖或蜂蜜。
・加牛奶打勻：取兩大匙地瓜泥，加入溫牛奶或豆漿，用果汁機打勻即可。
・加點小變化：撒一點肉桂粉或倒進一小份濃縮咖啡，就是自己的地瓜拿鐵。

不管是排隊買一杯新品，還是在家用電鍋蒸一條地瓜，冬天的甜味都很簡單。Cute News 覺得，捧著一杯紫色的溫暖，就是這個季節最可愛的小確幸。

posts.body:
一年一度的烏魚季又開跑了，剛捕獲的先頭烏和之後的正頭烏、回頭烏有什麼不同？這篇一次幫你整理清楚。
如果最近你在 50 嵐排隊時，聽到前面的人說「中杯波霸紅茶拿鐵，三分糖，溫的」，那麼他很可能正在進行一場可愛的「轉運儀式」。

這杯台灣人再熟悉不過的奶茶，這幾天在脆（Threads）上突然多了一個新身分：轉運神器。

## 從一句留言開始的「轉運奶茶」

根據 NOWnews 今日新聞與網路溫度計 DailyView 11 月 14 日的報導，事情起源於脆上一則提問：「有沒有人原本運氣很差，後來因為做了一件事，整個人生開外掛？」在一堆分享中，有位網友留言：「請去喝 50 嵐中杯波霸鮮奶茶，三分糖溫的，喝完即改運，只能在很衰的時候使用。」

這句帶點神秘感又很具體的留言，迅速在脆上擴散。DailyView 報導指出，流傳的截圖顯示這則留言累積超過 8,700 個讚；之後陸續有網友分享實測心得，其中一篇實測貼文也累積約 3.5 萬個讚。報導也引述 KEYPO 大數據觀測，11 月 12 日至 13 日短短 24 小時內，相關話題就累積了 1,106 筆網路聲量。

## 網友實測：有人說接到好消息，也有人笑說「冰的沒效」

留言區裡的分享五花八門：有人說喝完後卡關的專案突然有進展，有人說接到了新訂單，也有人開玩笑問：「我喝無糖的都沒怎樣，是不是一定要三分糖？」「喝冰的可以嗎？」這種一本正經研究細節的樣子，正是台灣網友最可愛的地方。

當然，轉運這件事信不信由你。比起真的改變運氣，這杯奶茶更像是一個小小的心理暗示：在覺得很衰的日子裡，給自己一個理由走出門、買一杯溫溫甜甜的飲料，對自己說一聲「沒關係，會好起來的」。

## 點單小提醒：正確名稱是「波霸紅茶拿鐵」

這波熱潮也讓店員們忙翻了。NOWnews 報導中，有店員提醒：50 嵐的菜單上並沒有「鮮奶茶」這個品項，點餐時請說**「波霸紅茶拿鐵」**，溝通會順利許多。也有店員笑說，最近爆紅飲品太多，「我看我們才更需要喝一杯來轉運一下」。

DailyView 也提到，這已經不是 50 嵐近期第一次因脆上推薦爆紅，前陣子才剛掀起「阿華田拿鐵加波霸」的熱潮。

## 跟風也要溫柔：Cute News 的 5 個小建議

- **報對品項名稱：**「中杯波霸紅茶拿鐵、三分糖、溫的」，一次說清楚，店員和後面的人都輕鬆。
- **尖峰時段多一點耐心：**熱門品項可能需要等，排隊時順便放空、深呼吸也很好。
- **甜度依自己身體調整：**轉運不一定要硬喝，喜歡無糖、微糖都可以，開心最重要。
- **自備環保杯：**喝飲料也愛地球，說不定運氣會更好。
- **對店員說聲謝謝：**他們才是這波熱潮背後最辛苦的人。

## 一杯溫奶茶，裝著台灣人的小幽默

從阿華田拿鐵到轉運奶茶，台灣人總能把一杯日常的手搖飲，變成大家一起參與的小遊戲。這種「明知道是玄學，還是想試試看」的可愛，正是生活裡的小確幸。

Cute News 想說，如果這週你也覺得有點衰，不妨去買一杯溫溫的波霸紅茶拿鐵，捧在手心暖暖的。運氣會不會變好不知道，但心情，一定會先好一點。

**Q：50 嵐轉運飲料怎麼點？**

A：源自 Threads 上一則詢問運氣翻轉經驗的貼文，有網友留言推薦這杯飲料「喝完即改運」，引發大量網友跟風實測與分享。

A：這是網友之間的趣味說法，沒有科學根據；不過在低潮時替自己買杯喜歡的飲料、轉換心情，也是一種溫柔的自我照顧。

posts.title: Always the organizer? 5 gentle manners for group trips, and why a simple reply means so much (inspired by a viral Threads post)
posts.body:
Translated from a Chinese-language article on Cute News, a Taiwanese lifestyle site.

Have you ever been the one who organizes the trip? You hunt for dates, check transport, book the restaurant and work out who owes what, quietly carrying everyone's plans on your own. The scariest part isn't that some people can't come — it's a group chat that goes completely silent. A story about a middle-school classmates' outing recently resonated with a lot of people on Threads. According to a roundup by *DailyView* (《網路溫度計 DailyView》), one user warmly started organizing a get-together and began asking everyone about their interest and availability in September. By November, many people were still leaving him on "read" without replying, and the organizer finally decided to cancel the trip. As of the morning of November 11, the post had collected about 93,000 likes and more than 3,300 comments.

## What really wears the organizer out is "no response"

The organizer later explained that what left him helpless wasn't people being unable to attend, but some members not replying for a long time and not offering any suggestions either, which made it hard to keep planning. Many people in the comments understood: "If you can't come, fine, but at least say so." "Having someone organize is a blessing." "You only know how tiring it is when you've organized a group where a bunch of people can't be bothered to reply."

In fact, most people who don't reply aren't being cold on purpose. They may be busy, haven't confirmed their schedule, or assume "someone else will answer first." But when everyone thinks that way, the organizer is left waiting in front of a silent screen. The good news is that with just a little more consideration, organizing a trip can become much easier.

## 5 gentle manners that keep group trips from being exhausting

**1. Organizers: set a reply deadline.** When you start the plan, write something like "please reply by Friday evening" and attach two or three date options or a poll, so people can decide at a glance.

**2. Saying "I can't make it" is also a good reply.** One line like "Can't do this time, have fun!" saves the organizer a lot of guessing. If you're not sure yet, "I'll get back to you by Wednesday" works great too.

**3. Don't just say "anything's fine."** "Anything's fine" sounds easygoing, but to the person planning it equals no information. Try offering a small suggestion, such as "I'd like hotpot" or "I'd prefer to leave in the afternoon."

**4. Share the work.** Reservations, transport research and collecting money can be handled by different people. The organizer doesn't have to do it all, and participants feel more involved.

**5. Remember to thank the organizer.** After the trip, saying "thanks for getting everyone together" in the group chat is the best motivation for the next gathering to happen.

## If you're the organizer: it's okay to gently let go

Some netizens suggested that when a group stays unresponsive for a long time, there's no need to force it. Organizers can shrink the gathering and go out first with the friends who do respond, or simply say lightly, "Let's pause this time, and meet up when everyone's free." People who are willing to organize are precious, and your time and effort deserve to be treated well too.

## A small gesture for participants

If you're the one being invited, besides replying on time, you can also ask once the plan is settled, "Is there anything I can help with?" Showing up on time on the day, settling costs on the spot, and sharing the nice photos you take in the group chat — these small details make the organizer feel it was all worth it, and let the next get-together happen more naturally.

As the year-end approaches, many people start arranging class reunions and small dinners before company year-end parties. The next time an invitation pops up in your group chat, try spending ten seconds to reply with a sentence. A tiny reply may be the reason a friendship keeps moving forward. Cute News wishes every organizer a group of friends who actually reply to messages.

*(Cover illustration in the original article: AI-generated illustrative image.)*

## FAQ

**Q: I received a trip invitation but I'm not sure whether I can go. How should I reply?**
A: You can reply first with "I'm still checking, I'll get back to you by Wednesday," so the organizer knows you've seen it and knows when to expect an answer.

**Q: How can an organizer reduce the number of people who leave the group on "read"?**
A: Include a reply deadline, concrete date options or a poll when you start the plan, and hand tasks like reservations and transport to different members.

**Q: How popular was this group-trip story?**
A: According to the *DailyView* roundup, as of the morning of November 11, 2026, the Threads post had about 93,000 likes and more than 3,300 comments.

posts.title: New in Taiwan cinemas on Nov 27: 'Bayside Shakedown N.E.W.', 'Meet the Fockers' sequel, restored 'A Room with a View' and more for a cosy winter weekend
posts.body:
Translated from a Chinese-language article on Cute News, a Taiwanese lifestyle site. Film titles are given as Taiwan release titles in Chinese with literal English glosses where no official English title was stated in the source.

When the weather turns cold, one of the best weekend plans is walking into a cinema holding a hot drink. This Friday, November 27, Taiwanese cinemas welcome several films that feel like "reuniting with old friends." Whether you like action, comedy, romance or music, there's something to pick.

## 《大搜查線 N.E.W.》 ("Bayside Shakedown N.E.W."): Aoshima Shunsaku is still a cop!

According to a report by Lang Lang Reading (琅琅悅讀), 《大搜查線 N.E.W.》, starring Japanese national actor Yuji Oda (織田裕二), is confirmed to open across Taiwan on November 27. Set in Tokyo, it follows Aoshima Shunsaku (青島俊作) taking up his post in the Metropolitan Police Department's First Investigation Division and facing the hardest case in its history.

"Bayside Shakedown" began as a Japanese TV drama in 1997. It not only depicts police investigations but also portrays the positions and struggles between the lower and upper ranks of a police organization. The first film in 1998 grossed more than 10 billion yen, and 2003's 《大搜查線 2：封鎖彩虹大橋》 ("Bayside Shakedown 2: Seal Off Rainbow Bridge") accumulated 17.35 billion yen. After this new film opened in Japan on September 18, it passed 3 billion yen in less than a month, with more than 2.14 million admissions. For longtime fans it's not just a detective film, but more like getting together again with an old friend you haven't seen in years.

## 《門當父不對之親家駕到》 ("Meet the Parents"-series sequel, literally "Fathers-in-Law Arrive"): from father-in-law vs. son-in-law to a clash of in-laws

TVBS News reports that the classic comedy series 《門當父不對》 returns with a sequel 16 years after its third film. Robert De Niro and Ben Stiller are back, and pop star Ariana Grande joins for the first time, playing "Olivia," the girlfriend of Ben Stiller's son. Unexpectedly, De Niro likes her very much, which makes her "future father-in-law" Ben Stiller suspicious.

Stiller shared that when he shot the first film he had just gotten engaged and was about to visit his future father-in-law; 26 years later he's the father of two grown children, who has gone from the son-in-law being put through the wringer to the father sizing up his son's partner. The producers also revealed that many Easter eggs from earlier films are hidden in it, making it a good one for the whole family to laugh together.

## 《窗外有藍天》 ("A Room with a View") 4K restoration: relive Florentine romance on the big screen

The classic literary film adapted from E.M. Forster's novel and directed by James Ivory is getting a new 4K restoration. Helena Bonham Carter plays Lucy, who meets George while travelling in Florence and finally bravely chooses to be true to her own heart. Its elegant imagery and literary feel suit a quiet winter afternoon.

## 《比爾艾文斯三重奏變》 (a film about Bill Evans and his trio): hearing equality and rapport in jazz

This film focuses on jazz pianist Bill Evans. In 1959 he took part in Miles Davis's legendary album *Kind of Blue*, and later formed a piano trio with bassist Scott LaFaro and drummer Paul Motian, letting every instrument converse freely. If you like jazz and stories about musicians, consider adding it to your schedule.

## Winter movie dates, planned

- **With old friends:** Watch 《大搜查線 N.E.W.》 together and chat afterwards about the days you used to follow the TV drama.
- **With family:** Choose 《門當父不對之親家駕到》, laugh, and then go for a hot dinner.
- **On your own:** Pick an afternoon for 《窗外有藍天》 or 《比爾艾文斯三重奏變》 and leave a little space for your heart.

## Cinema etiquette

Once inside, set your phone to silent and dim the screen, avoid bringing strong-smelling hot food, and during the end credits leave a little time so the film you love can linger in your mind a bit longer.

The cinema is a lovely winter shelter. This weekend, pick a film you like and spend two warm hours with someone important to you. (Showtimes, ratings and theatres are subject to each cinema's announcements.)

*(Cover illustration in the original article: AI-generated illustrative image.)*

## FAQ

**Q: When does 《大搜查線 N.E.W.》 open in Taiwan?**
A: According to the distributor's information, 《大搜查線 N.E.W.》 opens across Taiwan on Friday, November 27, 2026.

**Q: Who is in 《門當父不對之親家駕到》?**
A: It stars Robert De Niro and Ben Stiller, with pop singer Ariana Grande joining for the first time as Olivia, the girlfriend of Ben Stiller's son.

**Q: What else opens on November 27?**
A: Besides 《大搜查線 N.E.W.》 and 《門當父不對之親家駕到》, there are the 4K restoration of 《窗外有藍天》, 《比爾艾文斯三重奏變》 and 《綻放的巴黎之星》, among others. Please check each cinema's announcements for actual showtimes.

---

posts.title: What is a single grain whisky? A look at Bunnyville's No.17, a wheat whisky from Taiwan
posts.body:
Most people who start exploring whisky meet "single malt" first. "Single grain" shows up later, usually with a slightly puzzled look: if it's a single whisky, why isn't it malt? This post walks through what single grain whisky means, and then looks at one Taiwanese example, Bunnyville's No.17, using only what the distillery itself publishes.

## Single malt, single grain: what the words actually say

"Single" means the whisky comes from one distillery. The second word describes the grain behind it. Single malt is made from malted barley. Single grain is made from other grains — wheat, in the case of Bunnyville's No.17 — and, in the usual way of making it, is distilled in a column (continuous) still instead of only in pot stills. The result tends to be lighter and smoother, which is why grain whisky often ends up in blends and why a bottled single grain is an interesting thing to taste on its own.

## Where No.17 comes from

Bunnyville Distillery is in Guishan, Taoyuan, in a place locals call the "Rabbit Hole" (兔子坑). The distillery was licensed on July 15, 2004, which makes it one of Taiwan's first-generation private distilleries — the group of distilleries licensed between 2002 and 2004, right after the state monopoly on alcohol ended and private licences opened up.

No.17 got its name from an anniversary. According to the distillery's own product page, it is the inaugural single grain whisky, released to celebrate Bunnyville Distillery's 17th anniversary, and it is the first batch bottled after seven years of maturation in charred virgin American white oak barrels. The product page lists wheat as the grain, new American white oak as the cask, a 2017 distillation year and a 2023 bottling year.

## What the distillery says it tastes like

The official notes describe the aroma as subtle floral and honey notes, and the palate as apple, lemon and hazelnut. The distillery also calls the whisky smooth and accessible, and suggests it works on the rocks or in a Highball. That last point makes sense for a lighter, wheat-based whisky: there is less heavy malt character to fight against the soda, so the fruit and honey notes have room to show.

If you want to taste it the way the distillery describes it, here is a simple way to compare, without needing any special equipment:

1. **Neat or with one ice cube first.** Look for the floral and honey notes the label mentions, then the apple and lemon on the palate.
2. **Then try a simple Highball.** Use a tall glass, plenty of ice, whisky, and cold soda water poured gently down the side. The official notes name the Highball specifically, so it is the serve to test.
3. **Compare the two.** Notice which fruit note comes through more clearly when it is diluted and chilled.

[Image 2]

## The cask strength version

There is also a cask strength No.17. The distillery's page describes it as a combination of Canadian wheat and charred virgin American white oak barrels, aged for over seven years, bottled at 62.3%. The flavours listed are as sweet as milk chocolate, as rich as roasted chestnuts, with a hint of honey. It is the same grain and the same type of cask as the 40% version, but a single-cask, undiluted release, so it will taste noticeably bigger. If you try both, add a little water to the cask strength and see how the honey note changes.

## A short note on the column stills

Because single grain whisky is normally associated with column distillation, it helps to know what equipment Bunnyville lists. The distillery's website gives its distillation equipment as six pot stills (3,000, 2,000, 2,000, 1,000, 1,000 and 200 litres) and two column stills: one 7 metres tall with 20 bubble-cap plates, and one 9 metres tall with 32 bubble-cap plates. According to the site, a column with more plates separates more finely and gives a cleaner spirit, while a 20-plate column keeps more of the character of the raw material. The distillery does not say in these pages which still produced which whisky, so it would be a guess to link a particular bottle to a particular column.

The distillery also states its distilling capacity as one million bottles a year.

## Why single grain is worth a look

Single grain whisky is a small category in Taiwan, and Bunnyville's No.17 is a good entry point for three reasons:

- **It is easy to approach.** The official description emphasises smoothness, and the apple, lemon and hazelnut profile is quite different from a heavy malt.
- **It is a good Highball base.** The distillery itself recommends it.
- **It shows a different side of the same distillery.** Alongside its single malts finished in fruit and tea barrels, a wheat whisky aged in new American oak gives a useful comparison of what grain and cask each contribute.

If you want to see the bottles in person, the distillery lists a store at 1 Alley 13, Yongkang Street, Da'an District, Taipei. Check the official website for current opening details before you go.

*All facts above come from Bunnyville's own product and distillery pages; tasting notes are the distillery's official notes, not independent reviews.*
